title: Accessibility testing and progressive enhancement
learningObjectives: Explain accessibility testing and progressive enhancement and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: Accessibility testing combines semantic inspection, keyboard-only operation, visible focus, screen-reader checks, zoom and reflow, colour contrast, and automated checks. Progressive enhancement starts with meaningful content and native functionality, then adds JavaScript and advanced presentation without making the baseline unusable.
understand.whyItMatters: Automated tools catch only some issues. Manual testing reveals focus traps, confusing announcements, inaccessible custom controls, and broken reading order.
understand.analogy: Automated checks are a spell-checker; human testing is reading the page and trying to use it in real conditions.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The native label, input, and button provide a usable baseline. A complete page should also handle server validation and display accessible feedback.

examples.explanation: The native label, input, and button provide a usable baseline. A complete page should also handle server validation and display accessible feedback.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates the API or security principle; browser permission or environment support may be required.

practise.guidedTask: Test a form with keyboard only, browser zoom, and a screen reader. Record one issue found manually that an automated scan might miss.
practise.independentTask: Build a small browser feature using the API or safety principle. Test normal, denied, unavailable, and invalid cases where relevant.
hints: Treat data from the browser, URL, and network as untrusted.
Ask permission only after explaining the purpose.
Keep sensitive authorization and secrets on a trusted backend.

questions.prompt: Can an automated accessibility scan prove that a page is fully accessible?
options: No, manual testing with different interaction methods is also required
questions.answer: No, manual testing with different interaction methods is also required
questions.explanation: Automated scans detect only a subset of accessibility problems.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
